pain_points: Golf shop team cannot adapt to how phone calls need to be handled - Tom: 'we're struggling with our golf shop team right now'
The admin office was moved away from the golf shop during temporary relocations, so phone calls stopped being supported by the management team
Service quality varies by shift and by who picks up; Tom said of relying on human staff 'I can't rely on that right?'
Two people in the shop handle roughly 2,000-2,500 bookings a month with back-end support
Most inbound calls are rate-qualification calls (Hawaii resident rates are unpublished, industry rates, membership) that need research and rapport before a rate can be quoted
Phone accounts for 'at least 30 35% on a weekday' of bookings and about 60% at weekends, so call quality directly drives revenue

current_solution: Phones handled in-house by the golf shop: the Easy Links phone-call service was stripped away during COVID and the work moved into the shop. Two shop staff plus back-end support; the shop switches over to the call centre in the evening. Access tee sheet through Troon/Indigo Sports, with the Notify waitlist tool turned on. Fully prepaid online and through the call centre; phone bookings taken direct are paid at check-in. Tom and his assistant golf professional have built their own AI models over about three and a half years to encode the property's brand and sales flow.
features_demoed: Live AI voice call to an existing client course (The Divide, North Carolina) played over speaker
Weather forecast lookup mid-call before booking
Recovery when the caller changed the requested day, and a knowledge-base miss on practice facilities handled by offering to connect to the pro shop
Tee time search with nearby alternative times offered, and a course-condition heads-up about top dressing

Double-confirmation flow: full read-back of date, time, player count, holes, per-player and total price before locking in, built for the Divide's retirement-community clientele (sister course Highland Creek runs without it)
Cart inclusion, pay-at-counter, and SMS confirmation containing the booking link, a cancel link and a weather-guarantee upsell link

objections.trigger_quote: we're not as straightforward as as that booking, right?
objections.rep_response_summary: Elias said that the demoed call was only what a public booking sounds like and that CourseRev has many different setups across its courses, allowed that it might not be the exact one Tom had in mind, and asked Tom to walk through what his team asks a new caller in order to place them on the right rate.

objections.trigger_quote: we might not be the best client right from the get-go
objections.rep_response_summary: Elias said he was glad to hear it because CourseRev's big improvements come from iteration, and described the in-house tool that pushes all call logs through AI analysis to improve both the general system and specific properties.

objections.trigger_quote: the biggest thing here guys is are you willing to work with us to become customizable to the point where we deliver the message that we want to deliver?
objections.rep_response_summary: Elias said CourseRev will build anything as long as it is tenable, named the real limits (tech not being there, an integration layer being needed), cited the range of existing customer journeys from live a week after signing to three months of fine-tuning, and said they never want to be the reason a course is slow to go live. Tom had paired the question with an explicit alternative: if it is not possible he would keep building his own tooling and check back later.

objections.trigger_quote: is there a percentage model that we could come up with to where maybe it's a little bit more favorable for you guys up on the higher end
objections.rep_response_summary: Elias did not take up the percentage model. He clarified the charging basis instead: 'It's per round checked in.' - information calls, no-shows and cancellations are uncharged, and the fee only applies once a golfer checks in at the shop.

objections.trigger_quote: why don't you send me the legal agreement because I do need to I'm obviously these days I got to run it up to true and legal all that sort of stuff
objections.rep_response_summary: Bo committed to sending the agreement soon and offered to meet with any Troon department, legal included, if that would help move the approval along.

objections.trigger_quote: Another thing that may hold us up just a little bit, guys, is I have a new ownership um potential.
objections.rep_response_summary: Bo probed the timeline and established that the transition, if it happens, would land before the end of the year, then reframed it out of the immediate path: 'then we don't really need to loop in the new ownership yet because that's still roughly a couple months away'. Tom had flagged that some parties do not want contracts and legal agreements starting up now.

objections.trigger_quote: we got to have some boundaries in that too
objections.rep_response_summary: Elias said the boundaries would need to be defined more specifically, then laid out the range: the system can be set so CourseRev only sees incoming bookings; it works best with access to customer data so callers are recognised, but every call can instead come in fresh with CourseRev gathering phone number, email and payment details itself - 'We can be as blind as you you want us to be.' He added that their data analysis only aggregates bookings in house.

open.evidence: Tom opened already sold on the category: "myself and my assistant golf professional are locked in. We use AI all the time for everything that we're doing". He had done homework for the meeting - "I have actually prepped today by kind of putting together something." - and volunteered the pain unprompted: "we're struggling with our golf shop team right now".

post_demo.evidence: Engaged but with a clear caveat that the demoed flow was simpler than theirs: "we're not as straightforward as as that booking, right?" and "We don't know who our guest is until they call us and until we get into some research." He immediately added "I feel like I feel like the AI model can do it as long as it's trained to do it right." and took over the meeting to roleplay his own sales call for CourseRev to learn from.

at_pricing.evidence: Brief friction on the flat fee against low-value rounds - Tom asked "is there a percentage model that we could come up with to where maybe it's a little bit more favorable for you guys up on the higher end" and said "I'm worried that" about the lower end. Once Elias clarified the charge is per round checked in, Tom solved it himself: "any any round that could be considered complimentary tea time or something now just needs to have a little bit of a booking fee or something on top of that", then moved straight on to "the goal is for it to handle 95% of the phone calls".

close.evidence: Tom asked for the agreement unprompted and said "I really appreciate what you guys are doing. I think you guys got a lot of value" and "if it were up to just simply saying yes and going for it," "we would be already going for it". The holdups he named were external process, not reluctance, and he volunteered that CourseRev's Kapalua relationship helps: "It is good that you guys have something going with Capalooa" because "that'll make this a little easier".
